title: Dashboard ingestion holes and trace correlation corruption across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a set of customer escalations between 2026-02-27 and 2026-03-02, multiple tenants reported missing dashboard tiles, gaps in metric series, and broken trace/span correlations. The issue manifested across Hosted API, Dedicated pools experiencing autoscale events, and a subset of Private (VPC) deployments after a metadata propagation change. Users saw: missing CPU/RPS time series for 15-30m windows, dashboards failing to render due to 500 responses from the metrics aggregation service, and traces where span parent_ids were null after backend re-ingestion.

Impact: Several paying customers escalated (enterprise customers on Dedicated and three Private customers), leading to support tickets with P1 severity: inability to monitor SLAs, inability to use rollouts safely in Console, and one customer triggering a failover due to unclear metrics.

Root cause hypothesis (initial): A change deployed in metrics ingestion pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR/3812) introduced a race between the aggregator shard assignment code and the KV-config propagation used by Private control planes. When an autoscale event or control-plane config refresh occurred, some aggregator workers dropped index pointers for recently-written metric batches; reprocessing path corrupted trace parent linkage for spans that were in-flight. This was compounded by our dashboard renderer not tolerating partial series responses and returning a 500.

What we did so far:
- 2026-02-27 21:45 UTC: Support on-call triaged first report, created emergency incident channel (#incident-telemetry-20260227).
- 2026-02-27 22:10 UTC: Rolled back telemetry ingest change in Hosted (rollback PR github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR/3815). Immediate improvement observed for Hosted customers.
- 2026-02-28 01:30 UTC: For Dedicated pools, we applied a hotfix to aggregator workers to avoid dropping index pointers during shard moves (PR github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR/3820). Noticed partial recovery but some Private customers still affected.
- 2026-03-01 09:00 UTC: Identified config propagation gap in Private control plane (on-prem and VPC clients) where the new config key kv.metadata_version was not included in the propagation envelope used by the local aggregator. Opened PR to add compatibility shim (PR github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/PR/1156).
- 2026-03-02 17:00 UTC: Deployed a patch to dashboard renderer to fall back to partial-series rendering instead of failing hard (PR github.com/redwood-inference/console/PR/2244). Dashboards recovered for customers with intact underlying series.

Current plan (In Progress):
1) Stabilize Private deployments: ship the control-plane compatibility shim (PR 1156) to all affected customers via orchestrated upgrade (target 2026-03-12). The shim reintroduces the older metadata envelope for a 3-week compatibility window while we migrate aggregator logic.
2) Make aggregator re-ingestion idempotent and resilient: complete the aggregator reprocessing fix that ensures parent_id reconciliation when batches are replayed (PR github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR/3839). Rolling deploy across Hosted and Dedicated in staged waves.
3) Improve dashboard rendering fallback behavior and add explicit observability for partial responses so we can distinguish 'no data' from 'backend error'. Backfill dashboards to retry on transient 500s.
4) Create customer-facing incident summary and remediation timeline and share with impacted accounts by 2026-03-11 (responsible: CSM + Support).

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rollback for Hosted (complete).
- Hotfix on Dedicated aggregator workers (complete for primary clusters; secondary clusters scheduled).
- Dashboard renderer fallback deployed globally (console-2026.03 patch).
- Manual re-ingest initiated for the three most impacted Private customers (ticket assigned to SRE).

Testing and validation:
- Unit and integration tests added to telemetry repo to cover shard move + in-flight batch scenarios (tests/ingest_shard_move_test.go).
- End-to-end validation harness to simulate autoscale and control-plane upgrade flows created and added to nightly e2e (job: e2e-telemetry-stress).

Open risks and follow-ups: 
- Risk: The compatibility shim increases envelope size; still investigating impact on control-plane bandwidth for low-throughput Private networks.
- Follow-up: Add a dashboard-level synthetic probe that queries per-tenant series for a known probe metric to detect ingestion holes within 1 minute. (Follow-up ticket: ENG-17710).
- Follow-up: Postmortem doc (Confluence link below) due by 2026-03-18 with timeline, RCA, and recommendations for deployment gating.

Owner and escalation: Marek Novak (SRE) is the action owner for fixes and rollout. Escalation path: Aisha Patel -> Head of Platform Ops -> VP Eng.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident channel: https://slack.redwood/incoming/incident-telemetry-20260227
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood/internally/telemetry/PM-ENG-17623-draft
- Hosting rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/3815
- Aggregator hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/3820
- Control plane shim PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/1156
- Console fallback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2244

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- All impacted Private customers have ingested backfilled metrics and traces for the affected windows and confirm via CSM.
- No dashboard 500s for partial series within a 48h observation window after the final rollouts.
- New e2e stress test prevents regressions in pre-merge CI for telemetry changes.

Notes: This ticket consolidates multiple parallel remediation tasks and customer follow-ups. After the immediate fixes are complete we will split remaining hardening items into smaller follow-ups (ENG-17700, ENG-17701, ENG-17710).
